title: Claim: list-append-is-amortized-constant
body: List growth is geometric: capacity grows by a bounded fraction each time it is exceeded, so appends stay O(1) amortized.

title: Claim: list-pop-zero-scales-linearly
body: list.pop(0) cost grows with the list length, because every remaining pointer shifts.

title: Claim: deque-popleft-is-constant
body: deque.popleft cost does not grow with the deque length.

title: Claim: insort-shift-is-linear
body: bisect.insort is a binary search plus a list shift, so insertion at the front is linear; the search alone is logarithmic.

title: Q1: Why is list.pop(0) a poor choice for a BFS queue?
body:
A. It allocates a new list every time
B. It shifts every remaining pointer, so each pop costs O(n)
C. It is not allowed on lists
D. It is only slow for strings

**B.** A list is a contiguous array. Removing the first element moves each remaining pointer one slot left.

title: Q2: Which structure is the right queue for BFS in Python?
body:
A. list with pop(0)
B. collections.deque with popleft
C. dict with the smallest key
D. set with pop()

**B.** deque.popleft is O(1), because it touches only the block at the front.

title: Q3: Why are appends to a list amortized O(1)?
body:
A. Each append reserves exactly one slot
B. Capacity grows by a fraction each time it is exceeded, so copies are rare
C. Appends never copy
D. CPython stores lists as linked nodes

**B.** Spare capacity grows geometrically, so the cost of the occasional copy spreads across many appends.

title: Q4: bisect.insort on a sorted list is O(log n) per insert. True
body:
A. True: the binary search dominates
B. False: the search is O(log n) but the list shift makes insertion O(n)

**B.** Finding the position is logarithmic. Inserting the value shifts the elements after it.

title: Q5: Why can a list not be a dict key?
body:
A. Lists are too large
B. Lists are not hashable: their contents can change, so their hash would change too
C. Dict keys must be strings
D. Lists are stored out of order

**B.** A key's hash must stay constant while it is in the table. A mutable list cannot guarantee that.
